roles.name: Leader on Duty
roles.description: Leader responsible for the building while open.

roles.name: Truck Unload
roles.description: Unloads the trailer and sorts freight.

constraints.note: Try to leave 10 hours between shifts (avoid clopens).
Nobody works more than 5 days a week.
A leader on duty whenever the store is open.
Spread closes: at most 3 per person.
Spread opens: at most 3 per person.
Jordan and Casey shouldn't close together.

narrative:
Alright, here's the deal with Store #1123, Chicago IL. We've got the front end, GM, food, fulfillment, asset protection, the backroom crew, plus the leaders. Corporate keeps changing the planogram on us, but whatever. Shifts are at least 4 hours, nobody comes in for a 2-hour shift. Parking lot's been a mess since they repaved half of it. Reese R. likes being on truck unload, put them there when you can. There always has to be a leader on duty when we're open, one of the leaders. Terry T. is the best we've got with customers, honestly. And nobody does more than 10 hours in a day. Payroll is 1,451 hours this week. Can't go over without my DM signing off. We get freight Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays. The backroom crew starts at 4 in the morning on those days, wrapped by 10. I hate clopens. Try to give people 10 hours between a close and an open. The high schoolers and the college kids can't come in before 3 on weekdays. We just got through a remodel, so people are still finding stuff. No overtime, period. We're open 8am to 10pm, seven days. Keep Jordan C. and Casey W. on different shifts if you can, they don't get along.

We're in Chicago, so the schedule has to go up 14 days ahead, and changing it after it's posted costs us premium pay. Corporate posts it on time. A clopen with less than 10 hours between shifts gets paid at 1.25x for those hours here, so I'd rather not. Anyone on past 7.5 hours gets a 20-minute meal break, leaders too. Chicago minimum wage is $17.05; nobody here makes less than that.
